newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco arrests three Moslem fundamentalists - group.
newsitem.headline: Morocco arrests three Moslem fundamentalists - group.

text.p: Moroccan authorities have arrested three leaders of the outlawed Moslem fundamentalist group, al-Adl wal Ihsane, one day after they sought official authority to stage a protest march, a member of the group said on Sunday.
He named the three as Mohamed Alaoui, Fathallah Arslane and Abdelwahad al Moutwakel, members of the group's policy-making body, Majliss al Irchaad.

The spokesman, who asked not to be named, said the men were detained on Saturday, a day after they asked the authorities to allow al-Adl wal Ihsane's members to stage a march to protest at what he called the "siege" on the group's leader, Abdsalam Yassine.
It was not immediately possible to obtain official comment.
Yassine, now in his late 60s, was placed under house arrest at his home in the town in Sale, the twin city of the Moroccan capital, Rabat, on December 29, 1989.
The group was banned in January 1990, 10 years after it was founded. The authorities refused to recognise al-Adl wal Ihsane after it applied for official recognition in 1981.
